parts.title: SSC Reasoning: Syllogism & Venn Diagrams
parts.intro: Today we study 'Sets and Logic'. Syllogism (All/Some/No) tests your deductive reasoning. Venn diagrams help you visualize relationships between groups. In SSC, 'Basic Syllogism' and 'Logical Venn' are high-yield. Do you know why 'Some A are B' doesn't mean 'Some B are not A'? Let's master the circles today.

pages.title: Syllogism Basics
pages.intro: Syllogism uses two premises to reach a conclusion, drawn with circles representing groups.

branches.label: Some Not
branches.value: Part of first circle outside second

pages.title: Conclusion Rule
pages.intro: A conclusion is definitely true only if it holds in every possible diagram matching the statements.

blocks.text: A conclusion true in some diagrams but not all is NOT definitely true; SSC exams require truth across all possibilities.

pages.title: Logical Venn Diagrams
pages.intro: Circles show how sets relate; e.g., 'Fruits' contains 'Apples' and 'Mangoes' as separate inner circles.

blocks.text: A big circle 'Fruits' encloses smaller circles 'Apples' and 'Mangoes' without overlap, showing both are subsets but disjoint from each other.

pages.title: Common Relationships
pages.intro: Three key set relations: subset (all in), overlap (some common), disjoint (no common members).

rows: All members of one set are in the other
Some members common to both sets

pages.title: Data Venn
pages.intro: Overlapping circles show survey data; start from the center overlap to calculate exclusive counts.

cards.front: How do you represent 'All' in a syllogism diagram?
cards.back: Draw one circle completely inside another circle.

cards.front: How do you represent 'Some' in a syllogism diagram?
cards.back: Draw two circles that overlap each other.

cards.front: How do you represent 'No' in a syllogism diagram?
cards.back: Draw two separate circles that do not touch.

cards.front: How do you represent 'Some Not' in a syllogism diagram?
cards.back: Draw two circles where part of the first circle stays outside the second circle.

cards.front: When is a conclusion considered definitely true in a syllogism?
cards.back: A conclusion is true only if it is true in all possible diagrams.

cards.front: What term describes a relationship where every member of one group is also a member of another?
What term describes a relationship where two groups share some members?
What term describes a relationship where two groups have no members in common?
In Data Venn problems, where should you start your calculations?
cards.back: Always start with the overlapping region in the center.

cards.front: How do you find the number of people who only like one specific thing in a Data Venn diagram?
cards.back: Subtract the number in the overlap from the total given for that circle.

cards.front: If "All A are B" and "All B are C", then "All A are C"?
